content.text:
All findings hold on main. Here's the scope, sharpened against what actually shipped.

## What #540 changed for Option C

**The build phase is done.** #540 collapsed four build legs into `.github/actions/build-linux-image` and ratified it in a 160-line spec. Option C as written in the research doc ("declare the image set, derive every matrix") is now **partly obsolete and partly forbidden**:

| C's original scope | Status after #540 |
|---|---|
| Collapse build matrices (`build.yml:52-55`, `:230-233`, `release.yml:36-39`) | **Obsolete** — the shared action already prevents drift |
| Post-publish matrices (`record-image`, `update-description`) | **Untouched** — still the live defect |
| Emit build args from a manifest table | **Forbidden** — see below |

That last row matters. The new spec at `linux-image-build-boundary/spec.md:70-74`:

> Build arguments … SHALL be declared in the same workflow that names that Dockerfile, and **SHALL NOT be transported to it through a shared environment value assembled elsewhere.**

This is a deliberate reversal of the proposal's D2 (`BUILD_ARGS`). Whatever C does, it must not route build arguments through an `images[]` structure — that's now spec-violating. C is confined to **job topology**, not build inputs.

The spec also documents the collision I flagged (`:86-93`): `windows.git.version` is Git for Windows `2.55.0`, while `android.Dockerfile:10` declares `ARG GIT_VERSION` as a Debian apt pin `1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1` — same flat env name, different tools, different version grammars. And BuildKit only *warns* on an undeclared arg, so a misroute would be silent.

## Revised scope: post-publish only

```
BUILD PHASE                    POST-PUBLISH PHASE
(#540 — done)                  (Option C — the remaining work)
┌──────────────────────┐       ┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ build-linux-image    │       │ record-image      ✗ windows │ #506
│ action, 4 legs       │       │ update-description ✗ windows│
│ spec-ratified        │       │ cleanup-pr-image   ✗ web    │ tag leak
└──────────────────────┘       │ verify-published   ✓ (hand) │
                               └─────────────────────────────┘
   build ARGS: spec says            job TOPOLOGY: unowned
   "declare locally"                 nothing declares the set
```

Three findings confirmed still live on `main` at `05b2919`:
- `release.yml:186-187` — `update-description`, no windows
- `release.yml:236-237` — `record-image`, no windows (#506)
- `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26` — `PACKAGE_NAME: flutter-android`, so `flutter-web` PR tags leak
- `windows-image.yml` — still zero `outputs:` (C's prerequisite, untouched by #540)

## Recommended sequence

**1. `windows-image.yml` outputs** — small, standalone, unblocks everything else. Fixes the `verify-published` hardcode (`release.yml:169`) on its own merit.

**2. The `flutter-web` PR tag leak** — independent bug, no prerequisites, currently leaking. Doesn't need C at all.

**3. Option C (post-publish fan-out) + #506's documentation** — these merge naturally now. Once post-publish fans out over published images, `record-image` needs an explicit reason for excluding Windows, which is exactly the Option B content: `windows/amd64` unsupported, 5.90 GB over the 4 GB limit, no MSRC feed. The exclusion becomes a declared property of the image row rather than a silent matrix omission.

That's a genuinely better outcome than B alone — the skip gets *encoded*, not just commented.

One open question C must settle: whether the image set lives in `config/version.json` (my original suggestion) or somewhere separate. Given the new spec's insistence on keeping build args local to the building workflow, putting job-topology data in the same file that feeds build args risks re-creating the collision the spec just fenced off. Worth deciding in C's design rather than assuming.

Want me to write this up as C's proposal, or start with the `windows-image.yml` outputs change?
What's "The flutter-web PR tag leak"?

A bug I found during the Phase 0 exploration and mentioned in the research doc — but never explained end to end. Here it is.

`.github/workflows/cleanup-pr-image.yml` deletes the throwaway GHCR tags a PR creates once that PR closes. Line 26 hardcodes what it cleans:

```yaml
PACKAGE_NAME: flutter-android
```

That name is then the only thing it ever asks the GitHub API about (`:66`, `:82`) — list versions of package `flutter-android`, delete the matching `pr-<N>` one.

But PR builds push tags for **both** Linux images. `build.yml` fans out over `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`, and its GHCR tag push is per-`matrix.name`. So each PR creates two `pr-<N>` tags and the cleanup deletes one:

```
PR #123 opens
   ├─▶ ghcr.io/gmeligio/flutter-android:pr-123
   └─▶ ghcr.io/gmeligio/flutter-web:pr-123

PR #123 closes → cleanup-pr-image.yml
   ├─▶ deletes flutter-android:pr-123  ✓
   └─▶ flutter-web:pr-123 ────────────── never touched, stays forever
```

So every PR that has ever run a build has left a `flutter-web:pr-N` tag behind in GHCR, accumulating since `flutter-web` was added.

It's the same defect as #506 — a place that enumerates the image set by hand and was never updated when the second image arrived — which is why I grouped it with them. But it's independent work: no prerequisite, no relation to Docker Scout, and it's leaking right now. That's why I put it second in the sequence rather than folding it into Option C.

Two caveats on my confidence. I verified line 26 and the API calls directly on `main` just now. The "both images get PR tags" half I'm carrying from the structure agent's report (`build.yml:132-135`) and haven't re-read myself since #540 shifted that file — worth confirming before filing. And I haven't checked GHCR to count actual orphaned tags, so "accumulating forever" is inference from the code, not an observation.

Want me to confirm both, and check what's actually sitting in GHCR?

Both halves confirmed, and the leak is real and measured.

## Verified

**Code path** — `build.yml:48-55` matrixes both images; `IMAGE_REPOSITORY_PATH` derives from `matrix.name` (`:64`); metadata-action (`:132-138`) emits `ghcr.io/<owner>/<matrix.name>:pr-<N>`; both legs push. `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26` hardcodes `PACKAGE_NAME: flutter-android` and queries only that package (`:66`, `:82`).

**GHCR reality:**

| Package | Orphaned handoff tags |
|---|---|
| `flutter-android` | **2** (`pr-533`, `pr-543` — both open PRs, expected) |
| `flutter-web` | **22** (`pr-513` … `pr-543`) |

So `flutter-android` is clean — the two present are live PRs that haven't closed yet. Every closed PR's `flutter-web` tag is still there, back to `pr-513`. That's 22 orphans, and it grows by one per PR.

One correction to what I said earlier: I described these as accumulating "since `flutter-web` was added." The oldest orphan is `pr-513`, so either that's when web PR tags started or older ones were cleaned some other way — I didn't establish which, and it doesn't change the fix.

Worth noting what this costs beyond storage: each orphan is a full image index with SBOM and provenance attestations attached (`build.yml:151-155`), not a bare tag.

## Fix

Two lines, mechanically:

```yaml
strategy:
  matrix:
    package: [flutter-android, flutter-web]
env:
  PACKAGE_NAME: ${{ matrix.package }}
```

The tag-regex guard (`:49-52`) and the 404-idempotency case (`:88-90`) already handle a package that has no matching tag, so a matrix leg with nothing to delete exits cleanly at `:71-73`.

The 22 existing orphans need a one-off cleanup — the workflow only fires on `pull_request: closed` and `delete`, so it will never revisit them. Per your memory note, `tags == []` filtering is unsafe here (these are OCI indexes with attestation children); deleting by resolved version ID for a specific `pr-N` tag, as the workflow already does, is the safe path.

This is independent of #506 and Option C. Want me to file it as an issue, or open the PR?

content.text:
That settles it. Here's what I verified and what's genuinely open.

## Verified

**1. The manifest is machine-written, not hand-written.** `update-version.yml:348-375` composes it from three job outputs via `jq` overlays onto a base checkout. Renovate has no rule targeting `version.json` (grep found none) — the pipeline owns it end to end.

**2. The overlay is `. + $block` — a top-level merge.** Adding an `images` key is *safe* under it: `. + $a` replaces only the keys present in `$a` (`android`, `fastlane`), so `images` carries forward untouched from the base canvas. This was my main worry and it doesn't materialize.

**3. Every current key is a tool version.** `#Version` (`schema.cue:41-57`) is composed entirely of `#SemverPatch` / `#SemverMinor` / `#SemverQuad` / `#PlatformVersion`. There is no non-version concept in the file. An `images` array would be the first.

**4. The validation boundary is already right for this.** Consumers use `.github/actions/validate-version-manifest`; producers keep inline `cue vet` (`update-version.yml:100`, `:204`, `:300`). Either way `#Version` gates every write, so a new `#Image` definition would be enforced on every path with no new wiring.

**5. The collision the new spec fenced off is a naming collision, not a file collision.** `linux-image-build-boundary/spec.md:86-93`: `windows.git.version` (`2.55.0`) and `android.Dockerfile:10`'s `ARG GIT_VERSION` (Debian pin `1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1`) collide *after being flattened into env vars*. The manifest already holds values for both images without a problem — it's the flat env namespace that's unsafe. So my earlier caution ("putting job-topology data in the same file risks re-creating the collision") was **wrong**: an `images` array consumed via `fromJSON` into a matrix never passes through that namespace.

## What's missing to verify

Three things, and only one is a real blocker.

**A. Does the spec forbid this? — needs a judgment call, not a lookup.** `spec.md:70-74` says build arguments SHALL NOT be transported "through a shared environment value assembled elsewhere." An `images` array feeding `strategy.matrix` isn't a build argument and isn't an env value — so it reads as out of scope. But that spec was written days ago to close a specific hazard, and I'd rather have you confirm the intent than infer it. **This is the one that should gate the design.**

**B. Whether `cue vet` accepts the array shape.** `#PlatformVersion` proves arrays of structs validate fine (`schema.cue:45`), so I expect yes — but I haven't run `cue vet` against a draft `#Image` definition. That's a five-minute empirical check, not a design risk.

**C. Whether the post-publish jobs can actually consume it.** `fromJSON` into `strategy.matrix` requires the value to come from a job output, so a `setup`-style job would have to read the manifest and emit it — and `windows-image.yml` still declares no `outputs:`. This is the same prerequisite already at the top of the sequence, just re-confirmed from a second direction.

## Where I land

The file is fine. The real question isn't *where* the image set lives — it's whether `version.json` should hold non-version data at all, and that's a naming question about the file, not a safety one. If it grows an `images` key, "version manifest" becomes the wrong name for it.

Worth putting to you directly as C's first design decision: `images` inside `config/version.json` (one file, one validator, one loader, overlay-safe) versus a sibling `config/images.json` (keeps the version manifest purely about versions, costs a second schema and a second read). I'd lean to the former — the loader and the CUE gate already exist, and a second file is a second thing to keep in sync — but it's your call, and it's the decision that shapes the rest of C.

Verified. Every claim now has a test behind it.

## Results

| # | Claim | Method | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `images[]` validates under `#Version` | `cue vet` with a real `#Image` def | **PASS** |
| B2 | The schema actually constrains | 6 negative cases | **all 6 rejected**, valid control accepted |
| C1 | `. + $block` preserves `images` | Replayed `update-version.yml:356-370` | **survives all 3 overlays**, `cue vet` passes after |
| C2 | Payload feeds `strategy.matrix` | `jq` → `{include: [...]}` | **valid**, filters cleanly by `scan` / `runner` |
| C3 | Survives `GITHUB_OUTPUT` | Single-line round-trip | **1 line**, `fromJSON`-parseable |
| C4 | Derived legs match today | Diffed against all 5 matrices | **3 match exactly, 2 are the known bugs** |

That last row is the useful one. Deriving from a manifest reproduces `record-image`, `verify-published`, and the build legs **byte-for-byte** — and the only two places it disagrees are `update-description` (gains `flutter-windows`) and `cleanup-pr-image` (gains `flutter-web`), which are precisely the two defects. The change is behavior-preserving except where current behavior is wrong.

A `scan: bool` field also turns out to encode #506 exactly: `select(.scan)` yields today's `record-image` matrix, with Windows excluded *because the row says so* rather than because someone forgot. That's Option B's documentation and Option C's structure in one field.

**One correction to my earlier answer.** I said the negative tests passed on the first run — they hadn't. Python threw on bare `true` (JSON, not Python), so four cases silently re-validated a stale file and printed "rejected" for the wrong reason. The rerun above is the real result.

## Still unverified

**A — the spec-intent question, and it's yours to answer.** `linux-image-build-boundary/spec.md:70-74` forbids transporting build arguments "through a shared environment value assembled elsewhere." An `images` array feeding `strategy.matrix` is job topology, never touches a `--build-arg`, and never enters the flat env where `GIT_VERSION` collides. So it reads as out of scope — but that spec is four days old and written to close a hazard you'd just hit, so I'd rather you confirm than have me infer.

**Two things I did not test:** `fromJSON` in a live Actions matrix (this was local `jq`, not a real run), and whether `windows-image.yml` outputs work end to end — still zero `outputs:` there, still C's prerequisite.

**And the open design question stands**, now better informed: `images` in `config/version.json` versus a sibling `config/images.json`. The mechanics say the former is safe. The argument against is only naming — a file called `version.json` validated by `#Version` would hold something that isn't a version.

I'd take the single file. Your call, and it's C's first design decision.

content.text:
That settles A, and it overturns my own proposal.

## What `images[]` is actually for — and it mostly isn't

I proposed five fields. Checked against every consumer in the repo:

| Field | Consumers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | **30** `matrix.name` refs | Real |
| `target` | **3** `matrix.target` refs — all in Linux *build* legs | Owned by #540 |
| `dockerfile` | **0** — action hardcodes `file: android.Dockerfile` (`action.yml:68`) | **Dead** |
| `runner` | **0** — every `runs-on` is a literal; no job matrixes over it | **Dead** |
| `scan` | 0 today; would encode #506 | Speculative |

`docs/build.mjs:43` wants a bare string array. Every post-publish matrix carries **only `name`** — `update-description` (`:185-187`) and `record-image` (`:236-238`) have no second field at all.

So the honest shape is not a table of image tuples. It's **a list of names**:

```json
"images": ["flutter-android", "flutter-web", "flutter-windows"]
```

My `#Image` struct was designing for a generality nothing asks for. The `runner` field is the clearest tell — I put it there reasoning "Windows needs a different runner," but no job ever selects a runner from data; `windows-image.yml` hardcodes `windows-2025` because it *is* the Windows workflow. And `dockerfile` was dead the moment #540 hardcoded the path.

## And that reframes the spec question

I've been asking "does `spec.md:70-74` forbid an `images` array?" — the wrong question. The right one is what that requirement is *protecting*, and the spec says so plainly (`:84-93`): `config/version.json` holds values for two different images, two collide by name when flattened (`windows.git.version` vs `android.Dockerfile`'s Debian `ARG GIT_VERSION`), and BuildKit only warns on an undeclared arg — so a misroute is silent.

The hazard is **flattening into a shared namespace**. A list of names feeding `strategy.matrix` never flattens, never becomes a `--build-arg`, never enters the env where `GIT_VERSION` lives. My five-field struct was closer to the hazard — `target` and `dockerfile` *are* build inputs, and routing them through a manifest is exactly the indirection `:72-74` rejects. A name list isn't.

So I'd now answer A myself, with a caveat: the spec doesn't forbid this, and the narrower shape isn't merely permitted — it's the one that stays clear of the hazard. What I can't verify is whether you'd *want* the file to hold non-version data at all. That's taste about the file's identity, not safety.

## Revised

What #506 needs is much smaller than Option C as written:

- A list of names in the manifest (or a sibling file), consumed by the post-publish matrices and `cleanup-pr-image.yml`
- Windows's Scout exclusion recorded as a documented reason, not a `scan: bool` — one boolean read by one job is thinner justification than a comment citing `windows/amd64`, 5.90 GB, and the missing MSRC feed

Drop `dockerfile`, `runner`, and `target` outright. Build-phase concerns are #540's, and it settled them.

This also weakens my earlier lean toward `config/version.json`. A bare name list has no schema affinity with `#Version` — it isn't a version — so `config/images.json` costs less than I implied: one small CUE def, one read, and the version manifest stays honestly named. I'd now call it close to even, leaning slightly to the separate file.

Worth noting: my negative tests validated a schema I'm now discarding. They proved CUE *can* enforce that shape, not that the shape is right — a distinction I should have drawn before writing them.
OK for config/images.json
Decision noted: `config/images.json`, bare name list. Let me capture what this exploration actually established, since the research doc on disk still says something different.

# Addendum — after #540 (2026-08-10)

PR #540 (`refactor(ci): share one Linux image build step across the four build
legs`, merged at `05b2919`) landed between the exploration above and this
addendum. It changes what remains of Option C, and several claims above are
now superseded. Read this section as authoritative where the two conflict.

## What #540 changed

It shipped a different shape than its own proposal described. The proposal's
D2 (a `BUILD_ARGS` newline string emitted by `setEnvironmentVariables.js`) was
**dropped**. What shipped instead:

- `.github/actions/build-linux-image/action.yml` — a composite action owning
  the whole `docker/build-push-action` invocation, including all seven build
  args inline. Used by all four Linux legs.
- `.github/actions/validate-version-manifest/action.yml`
- `script/setEnvironmentVariables.js` — a `read()` helper that throws a named
  error on an unresolvable manifest path
- `openspec/specs/linux-image-build-boundary/spec.md` (160 lines), ratifying
  the above

**Consequence for the "12 enumerations" finding:** the build-phase duplication
is gone. `build.yml`, `ci.yml`, and `release.yml` no longer restate build args.
What remains is the **post-publish** fan-out, which #540 did not touch —
verified at `05b2919`: `release.yml:186-187` (`update-description`),
`release.yml:236-237` (`record-image`), `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26`.

## The `flutter-web` PR tag leak — confirmed empirically

Listed above as an unfiled sibling; now measured against GHCR.

`build.yml:48-55` matrixes both Linux images; `IMAGE_REPOSITORY_PATH` derives
from `matrix.name` (`:64`); metadata-action (`:132-138`) emits
`ghcr.io/<owner>/<matrix.name>:pr-<N>`. Both legs push.
`cleanup-pr-image.yml:26` hardcodes `PACKAGE_NAME: flutter-android` and
queries only that package (`:66`, `:82`).

| Package | Orphaned handoff tags in GHCR |
|---|---|
| `flutter-android` | 2 (`pr-533`, `pr-543` — both open PRs, expected) |
| `flutter-web` | **22** (`pr-513` … `pr-543`) |

Each orphan is a full image index with SBOM + provenance attestations
(`build.yml:151-155`), not a bare tag. Fix is a two-line matrix over the
package name; the existing tag-regex guard (`:49-52`) and 404-idempotency
case (`:88-90`) already handle a leg with nothing to delete. The 22 existing
orphans need a one-off cleanup — the workflow fires only on
`pull_request: closed` and `delete`, so it will never revisit them.

Independent of #506 and of Option C. No prerequisites.

## What the image set actually needs to carry

The exploration above assumed a table of image tuples
(`{name, dockerfile, target, runner, testConfig}`). Checked against every
consumer in the repo at `05b2919`, most of those fields have no reader:

| Field | Consumers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | 30 `matrix.name` references | Real |
| `target` | 3 `matrix.target` refs, all in Linux *build* legs | Owned by #540 |
| `dockerfile` | 0 — `build-linux-image/action.yml:68` hardcodes `file: android.Dockerfile` | Dead |
| `runner` | 0 — every `runs-on:` is a literal; no job matrixes over it | Dead |
| `scan` | 0 today; would encode #506's exclusion | Speculative |

Every post-publish matrix carries **only `name`** — `update-description`
(`release.yml:185-187`) and `record-image` (`:236-238`) have no second field.
`docs/build.mjs:43` wants a bare string array.

So the honest shape is a list of names, not a table:

```json
["flutter-android", "flutter-web", "flutter-windows"]
```

A `scan: bool` field was considered to encode #506's exclusion and rejected:
one boolean read by one job is thinner justification than a comment citing
`windows/amd64`, 5.90 GB, and the absent MSRC feed.

## Does `linux-image-build-boundary` forbid this? No.

`spec.md:70-74` forbids transporting build arguments "through a shared
environment value assembled elsewhere". The hazard it protects against is
stated at `:84-93`: `config/version.json` holds values for two images, two
collide once flattened into env (`windows.git.version` = `2.55.0` vs
`android.Dockerfile:10`'s `ARG GIT_VERSION` = Debian pin
`1:2.47.3-0+deb13u1`), and BuildKit only *warns* on an undeclared build arg,
so a misroute is silent.

The hazard is **flattening into a shared namespace**. A list of names feeding
`strategy.matrix` never flattens, never becomes a `--build-arg`, and never
enters the env where `GIT_VERSION` lives. The originally-proposed tuple was
closer to the hazard — `target` and `dockerfile` *are* build inputs, and
routing them through a manifest is the indirection `:72-74` rejects. A name
list is not.

## Decision: `config/images.json`

A bare name list has no schema affinity with `#Version` — it is not a version
— so it lives in its own file rather than in `config/version.json`. Cost: one
small CUE definition and one read. Benefit: the version manifest stays
honestly named, and the image set is not subject to the `jq` overlay in
`update-version.yml:348-375`.

Verified mechanics (local, at `05b2919`):

- `cue vet` accepts an array-of-structs under a root definition; 6 negative
  cases (bad enum, missing required field, duplicates, empty array, wrong
  scalar type, pattern violation) all rejected, valid control accepted.
  *(These tested the richer `#Image` struct since discarded — they prove CUE
  can enforce such a shape, not that the shape is right.)*
- `jq -c '{include: [...]}' ` produces a valid `strategy.matrix` payload that
  survives a single-line `GITHUB_OUTPUT` round-trip and parses under
  `fromJSON`.
- Derived legs vs. today's hardcoded matrices: `record-image`,
  `verify-published`, and the build legs reproduce **exactly**; the only two
  disagreements are `update-description` (gains `flutter-windows`) and
  `cleanup-pr-image` (gains `flutter-web`) — precisely the two known defects.
  The change is behaviour-preserving except where current behaviour is wrong.

**Not yet verified:** `fromJSON` in a live Actions matrix (the above is local
`jq`, not a real run), and `windows-image.yml` outputs end to end — that
workflow still declares zero `outputs:` at `05b2919`.

## Revised sequence

1. **`windows-image.yml` gains `outputs:`** — small, standalone, unblocks the
   rest. Fixes the `verify-published` hardcode (`release.yml:169`) on its own
   merit.
2. **The `flutter-web` PR tag leak** — independent, no prerequisites,
   currently leaking. Plus the one-off cleanup of the 22 orphans.
3. **`config/images.json` + post-publish fan-out + #506's documentation** —
   these merge naturally: once post-publish derives its legs from the list,
   `record-image` needs an explicit reason to exclude Windows, which is
   exactly Option B's content. The exclusion becomes stated rather than
   silently absent.

Step 3 still requires amending
`openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md:65,82`, which normatively
ratifies the skip on `needs:` topology rather than on Scout's platform
support.

## Next steps

Run `/opsx:propose` for step 1 (`windows-image.yml` outputs) or step 2 (the
tag leak) — both are independent of the Scout question. Step 3 is where this
research doc's Option B content lands.

input.content:
## Why

This project publishes three images. Nothing declares that. The set is
re-typed by hand in every job that fans out over it, and the copies have
drifted — three times, in three different directions:

- `record-image` (`release.yml:236-238`) omits `flutter-windows`, so the
  Windows image has never been recorded in Docker Scout ([#506]).
- `update-description` (`release.yml:185-187`) omits it too, so the Windows
  image's Docker Hub page is never synced from `readme.md`.
- `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26` hardcodes `flutter-android`, so every closed PR
  leaves a `flutter-web:pr-<N>` tag behind. Measured against GHCR on
  2026-08-10: **22 orphans** (`pr-513` … `pr-543`), each a full image index
  carrying SBOM and provenance attestations. `flutter-android` has 2, both
  live PRs.

One job got it right, and its comment (`release.yml:137-141`) is a post-mortem
of this exact failure, written before #506 was filed:

> "Did it publish?" is read from the registry by an anonymous pull, never
> inferred from which release job succeeded — that coupling is what let this
> job drift before.

That lesson was applied to one job out of four. PR #540 fixed the same defect
on the *build* side by giving the four Linux build legs one shared action.
Post-publish still has nothing equivalent.

Relevance gate: this changes what a CI engineer observes about the published
Windows image — whether its Docker Hub page matches the others, and whether
its absence from the code-scanning dashboard is a stated decision or an
accident. It also stops a registry leak that is live today.

## What Changes

- **`config/images.json`** — a new file holding the published image set as a
  list of names, validated by a new CUE definition. Separate from
  `config/version.json` on purpose: a name list is not a version, and
  `#Version` should not grow a member that isn't one.
- **`windows-image.yml` gains `outputs:`** — it is the repo's only
  `workflow_call` workflow and today returns nothing, so no caller can read
  what it published. This is what lets post-publish jobs stop guessing.
- **Post-publish jobs derive their matrices** from the declared set instead of
  restating it: `update-description`, `record-image`, `verify-published`.
- **`cleanup-pr-image.yml` iterates the set**, and the 22 existing orphans are
  swept once — the workflow fires only on `pull_request: closed` and `delete`,
  so it will never revisit them.
- **`flutter-windows`'s exclusion from Scout becomes stated**, with its three
  verified reasons, rather than being a silent gap in a matrix.

Explicitly **not** in scope, stated so it is not mistaken for an omission:

- Build-phase enumeration. PR #540 settled it; `linux-image-build-boundary`
  ratifies it. Build arguments SHALL NOT be routed through this file — that
  is the hazard `linux-image-build-boundary/spec.md:70-74` exists to prevent.
- Adding a Windows-capable vulnerability scanner. Researched and rejected:
  see below.
- `docker-compose.yml` and `docs/build.mjs`, which also enumerate images.
  They are correct today; folding them in can follow once the file exists.

### Why `flutter-windows` is excluded from Scout rather than added to it

[#506] asks to verify whether Scout produces meaningful output for the Windows
image before wiring it up. It does not, on three independent grounds — any one
of which is disqualifying:

1. **Architecture.** Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only
   ([docs](https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/)). The published image
   is `os: windows, arch: amd64` — read from its registry config blob, not
   inferred. Not fixable: Windows containers are `windows/amd64` by
   construction.
2. **Size.** The same limit is 4 GB compressed. The published image is
   **5.90 GB across 37 layers**, the `servercore` base alone being 1.42 GB.
3. **No data, and no package inventory to apply it to.** Scout's 23 advisory
   sources include no Microsoft/MSRC feed, and every OS ecosystem it supports
   is a Linux one
   ([sources](https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/)).
   Nor would a different scanner help: `windows.Dockerfile` installs Git from
   a zip (`:20`), Flutter via `git clone` (`:42`), and VS Build Tools via an
   installer (`:74`). None is registered with any package manager, so an
   SBOM-driven scanner finds an empty inventory. Trivy's supported-OS table
   has no Windows row; Grype delegates cataloguing to Syft, which has no MSI
   or KB cataloger.

Windows CVE posture is therefore governed by the `servercore:ltsc2025` digest
pin (`windows.Dockerfile:3`) and how promptly it is bumped — Microsoft
rebuilds monthly on Patch Tuesday — not by code scanning.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `published-image-set`: which images this project publishes, declared once;
  how jobs that act on every published image derive their legs from that
  declaration; and how an image that is deliberately out of scope for a
  post-publish step records why.

### Modified Capabilities

- `ci-image-tag-lifecycle`: its Purpose and every requirement are scoped to
  `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android` (`spec.md:5,11,17,43`). That scope is the
  spec-level form of the leak — `flutter-web` handoff tags are equally
  temporary and equally in need of deletion.
- `windows-image-release`: `spec.md:65,82` normatively require `record-image`
  to be **skipped**, justified by `needs:` topology. The skip is right; the
  justification is not. It must rest on Scout's platform support, so the
  requirement survives the post-publish jobs no longer hanging off
  `release-linux`.

## Impact

**New**: `config/images.json`; a CUE definition validating it.

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/windows-image.yml` (`outputs:`);
`.github/workflows/release.yml` (`verify-published`, `update-description`,
`record-image`); `.github/workflows/cleanup-pr-image.yml` (matrix).

**One-off**: sweep the 22 orphaned `flutter-web` handoff tags. Per
`feedback_ghcr_untagged_filter`, deletion must resolve a specific `pr-<N>` tag
to a version ID — a `tags == []` filter would match OCI index children and
break parent tags.

**Verification**: derived legs were diffed against today's hardcoded matrices.
`record-image`, `verify-published`, and the build legs reproduce **exactly**;
the only two disagreements are `update-description` (gains `flutter-windows`)
and `cleanup-pr-image` (gains `flutter-web`) — precisely the two defects. The
change is behaviour-preserving except where current behaviour is wrong.

**Risk**: `fromJSON`-driven matrices have been verified locally with `jq`
(valid payload, single-line `GITHUB_OUTPUT` round-trip) but not yet in a live
Actions run. First PR proves it on one job before the rest depend on it.

**Sequencing** — three PRs, split on real dependencies, not on convenience:

| PR | Scope | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `windows-image.yml` outputs | — |
| 2 | Tag-leak matrix + orphan sweep | — |
| 3 | `config/images.json` + post-publish fan-out + #506 exclusion | PR 1 |

PRs 1 and 2 are independent of each other and can land in either order. PR 2
fixes a live leak and is worth landing first regardless. PR 3 needs PR 1
because a post-publish job cannot fan out over the Windows image until
`windows-image.yml` reports what it published.

[#506]: https://github.com/gmeligio/flutter-docker-image/issues/506

# published-image-set Specification

## Purpose

Declare which images this project publishes, once, and derive from that
declaration every job that acts on all of them — verifying publication,
syncing registry descriptions, recording vulnerability data, and deleting
temporary tags. Covers where the set is declared, how a job that acts on every
published image obtains its legs, and how an image deliberately out of scope
for one of those steps records why. The experience context is the CI engineer
who pulls `flutter-windows` expecting the same treatment `flutter-android`
gets — a matching Docker Hub page, a stated security posture — and the
maintainer who adds a fourth image and needs it to reach every step without
finding them by hand.

## Requirements

### Requirement: The published image set is declared once

The set of images this project publishes SHALL be declared in one file,
`config/images.json`, and SHALL be schema-validated on every path that writes
it.

A workflow that acts on every published image SHALL derive its legs from that
declaration. It SHALL NOT restate the set inline.

The declaration SHALL carry image names only. Build inputs — Dockerfile paths,
build stages, build arguments — SHALL NOT be routed through it: those belong
to the workflow that names the Dockerfile they feed
(`linux-image-build-boundary`), and transporting them through a shared
structure is the indirection that spec exists to prevent.

**Experience context:** A maintainer adding a fourth image edits one file and
every post-publish step picks it up. Before this requirement the set was
re-typed in each job, and three copies had drifted: `record-image` and
`update-description` both omitted `flutter-windows`, and `cleanup-pr-image`
named only `flutter-android`. Each omission was invisible unless someone
diffed the matrices by hand — and each was found only after it had been wrong
for months.

#### Scenario: A newly declared image reaches every post-publish step

- **GIVEN** a maintainer adds an image name to `config/images.json`
- **WHEN** the release workflow next runs
- **THEN** the image is verified, its registry description is synced, and its temporary tags are eligible for cleanup
- **AND** no workflow file required a matrix edit for it to be included

#### Scenario: The declaration is validated before it is used

- **GIVEN** `config/images.json` contains a malformed or empty set
- **WHEN** validation runs
- **THEN** it fails naming the file
- **AND** no job fans out over an unvalidated set

#### Scenario: Build inputs are not carried by the declaration

- **GIVEN** the declaration is read by a workflow
- **WHEN** a maintainer inspects what it provides
- **THEN** it yields image names only
- **AND** no build argument, Dockerfile path, or build stage is obtained from it

### Requirement: Every published image is verified, described, and tag-cleaned

Each image in the declared set SHALL be verified as anonymously pullable after
release, SHALL have its registry description synced from `readme.md`, and
SHALL have its temporary handoff tags (`pr-<N>`, `branch-<branch>`) deleted
when the PR closes or the branch is deleted.

A post-publish job SHALL derive which images to act on from the declared set,
not from which build job produced them.

**Experience context:** A CI engineer pulling `flutter-windows` from Docker
Hub sees the same description the other images carry, rather than an empty
page — the Windows image is published by a different job, not held to a
different standard. And a maintainer browsing GHCR does not find dead tags
from PRs closed months ago: on 2026-08-10 `flutter-web` carried 22 orphaned
handoff tags (`pr-513` … `pr-543`), each a full image index with SBOM and
provenance attestations, because cleanup named only `flutter-android`.

#### Scenario: A closed PR leaves no handoff tag on any image

- **GIVEN** a PR that built every image that produces handoff tags
- **WHEN** the PR closes
- **THEN** each image's `pr-<N>` tag is deleted
- **AND** no image retains a handoff tag because cleanup did not name it

#### Scenario: The Windows image's Docker Hub page matches the others

- **GIVEN** a release publishes `flutter-android`, `flutter-web`, and `flutter-windows`
- **WHEN** description sync runs
- **THEN** every published image's Docker Hub description is updated from `readme.md`
- **AND** none is skipped for being built by a different job

#### Scenario: Release tags are never a cleanup target

- **GIVEN** cleanup runs for any image in the declared set
- **WHEN** it computes the tag to delete
- **THEN** only `pr-<N>` and `branch-<branch>` tags are reachable
- **AND** a release tag or `buildcache` is refused before any deletion is attempted

### Requirement: The Windows image build reports what it published

The reusable workflow that builds the Windows image SHALL declare outputs
identifying what it produced — at minimum the published image name and tag.

**Experience context:** A maintainer adding a post-publish step reads the
producing workflow's outputs to learn what it published, rather than
re-deriving the name from memory. Today that workflow declares none, so
`verify-published` works only because someone typed `flutter-windows` into its
matrix by hand — the same class of hand-copying that produced three drifted
matrices elsewhere. This mirrors `ci-image-handoff`, which already requires
the PR-path build job to expose its outputs for exactly this reason.

#### Scenario: A caller can read what the Windows build published

- **GIVEN** a workflow calls the Windows image build
- **WHEN** the call completes
- **THEN** the caller can read the published image name and tag from its outputs
- **AND** does not restate either value to use it

### Requirement: An image out of scope for a post-publish step records why

When an image in the declared set is deliberately excluded from a post-publish
step, the exclusion SHALL be recorded with its reason at the point of
exclusion. An image SHALL NOT be excluded by being absent from a list.

**Experience context:** A maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` missing
from the code-scanning dashboard finds a stated reason instead of filing the
bug again. `flutter-windows` is excluded from Docker Scout because Scout
analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only while the image is
`windows/amd64`; because the image is 5.90 GB compressed against a 4 GB limit;
and because Scout carries no Microsoft advisory feed and the image installs
its tools outside any package manager, so no SBOM-driven scanner — Scout,
Trivy, or Grype — would find an inventory to match against. Its CVE posture is
governed by the `servercore` base-image digest pin and how promptly it is
bumped.

#### Scenario: A deliberate exclusion is distinguishable from an oversight

- **GIVEN** a maintainer reads the job that records images in Docker Scout
- **WHEN** they ask why `flutter-windows` is not among its legs
- **THEN** the exclusion and its reason are stated where the legs are derived
- **AND** the reason cites the platform limitation, not which job built the image

#### Scenario: Excluding one image from one step does not exclude it from others

- **GIVEN** `flutter-windows` is out of scope for vulnerability recording
- **WHEN** the other post-publish steps run
- **THEN** it is still verified as pullable and still has its description synced
- **AND** the exclusion is scoped to the step that declared it

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only

The `release.yml` workflow SHALL continue to declare `workflow_dispatch:`. On `workflow_dispatch`, only the `release-windows` caller job SHALL execute; the Linux release job and the post-publish jobs that depend on a Linux publish (`update-description`, `create-github-release`) SHALL be skipped. The `FLUTTER_VERSION` env var SHALL be set from `github.ref_name`, so that a maintainer can rebuild a single tag's Windows image — through the same `windows-image.yml` reusable workflow — without re-cutting the Git tag and without re-publishing the Linux images, re-pushing the Docker Hub readme, or re-attempting `gh release create`.

Skipping SHALL be expressed as an explicit event guard, not inferred from a `needs:` edge to whichever job happens to build the Linux images. Post-publish jobs derive their legs from the declared published image set (`published-image-set`), so a `needs:` edge no longer determines which images a step covers.

The experience context is the maintainer recovering from a transient Windows runner failure: they re-run the workflow on the existing tag instead of force-pushing a new one. Linux recovery, by contrast, is the established fix-forward + re-tag pattern and does not need a `workflow_dispatch` path.

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild produces a fresh Windows image

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists in the repository
- **AND** the prior `release-windows` run for that tag failed
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the `release-windows` caller builds and pushes `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` to all three registries via `windows-image.yml`
- **AND** the existing Windows image digests at those tags are overwritten by the new digests

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild leaves the Linux digests untouched

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists and was previously published with Android digest `D_a`
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the Linux release job is reported as `skipped`
- **AND** `update-description` and `create-github-release` are reported as `skipped`
- **AND** the digest at `docker.io/<org>/flutter-android:X.Y.Z` remains `D_a`
- **AND** the run is reported as success (no failed jobs)

### Requirement: The Windows image is out of scope for Docker Scout

`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, and the exclusion SHALL be justified by Scout's analysis support rather than by which job builds the image.

Three independent facts each make the analysis impossible, and they SHALL be recorded where the exclusion is expressed: Docker Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images only, while the published image is `windows/amd64`; the analysis size limit is 4 GB compressed, while the published image is 5.90 GB; and Scout carries no Microsoft advisory feed, while the image installs Git, the Flutter SDK, and VS Build Tools outside any package manager, so no SBOM-driven scanner finds an inventory to match against.

The Windows image's CVE posture is instead governed by the `servercore` base-image digest pin in `windows.Dockerfile` and how promptly that pin is bumped.

The experience context is the maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` absent from the code-scanning dashboard: they find a stated reason and a pointer to what does govern its CVE posture, instead of re-filing a bug that was already investigated.

#### Scenario: The exclusion is stated, not implied by absence

- **GIVEN** a maintainer reads the job that records images in Docker Scout
- **WHEN** they ask why `flutter-windows` is not among its legs
- **THEN** the exclusion is expressed at the point where the legs are derived, with its reason
- **AND** the reason cites Scout's platform and size limits and its advisory coverage, not the release topology

#### Scenario: The Windows image is still covered by the other post-publish steps

- **GIVEN** `flutter-windows` is out of scope for Docker Scout
- **WHEN** a release publishes it
- **THEN** it is still verified as anonymously pullable
- **AND** its Docker Hub description is still synced from `readme.md`

begins. Never edits code, and never edits the artifacts under review.

If a name is provided, use it. Otherwise:

### 2. Collect the artifacts

```bash

```

From the JSON take:

- `artifactPaths.<id>.existingOutputPaths` — the concrete files on disk, already

needs them to detect contradiction and duplication.

If no artifacts exist, report that and point the user at `/opsx:propose`. This is
a warning, not a hard failure.

### 3. Load the project's review criteria

Read `openspec/config.yaml` from the project root and take:

- `context` — project background and what tends to go wrong here
- `rules.proposal` — the relevance gate, when the project defines one
- `rules.specs` — what this project requires of a spec

These are the project's philosophy. Pass them to the subagent as criteria
alongside the cross-artifact checks in step 4. Do NOT restate spec-philosophy
checks in this skill — traceable value, load-bearing guardrails, scope breadth
and their kind live in the project's config, and a second copy here would take
precedence over the file the developer edits.

Note which of the three keys were actually found. Step 7 reports this.

When the project has no `openspec/config.yaml`, continue with the cross-artifact
checks alone and record that no project philosophy was available. Warning, not
hard failure.

### 4. Dispatch the review

Use the Agent tool (`subagent_type: "general-purpose"`).

**Pass artifact content only. Never pass conversation history, your own
reasoning, or why any artifact was written the way it was.** The agent that wrote
a proposal is the worst reviewer of it: given its own rationale it will
reconstruct and defend the intent rather than read what the page says, and the
review degrades into agreement — worse than no review, because it carries the

Report findings in three severities.

CRITICAL — implementation would be wrong:
- A task implements behavior no requirement states
- A delta spec contradicts a main spec requirement without a MODIFIED or
  REMOVED marker
- A design decision makes a stated requirement unimplementable
- A required artifact is missing entirely
- Any violation of the project criteria the criteria themselves mark CRITICAL

WARNING — the plan is weaker than it should be:

- A design decision is stated with no rationale

Show the developer:

**BLOCKED** — list the CRITICAL issues and ask what to fix. Write no marker. Once

- Reviews only: never edit implementation code, and never edit the artifacts

## Review result: BLOCKED

**Criteria source:** all three loaded — `context`, `rules.proposal`, `rules.specs` from `openspec/config.yaml`.

### CRITICAL

**1. Contradicts `ci-image-anonymous-availability` with no MODIFIED delta.** That spec (`:64-70`) requires the opposite of what my delta requires:

> `verify-published` SHALL gate each image's checks on the result of the release job that produces it, so that a partial or platform-scoped release verifies only the images it published.

A static `config/images.json` cannot shrink to what a partial run published, so its `workflow_dispatch` scenario (`:76-82`) becomes unimplementable. This trips `config.yaml:21` — *"Reject if change contradicts an existing spec's experience impact"*. Worse, my task 5.3 files this as a follow-up, which doesn't license shipping the contradiction now.

**2. Four task citations point at the wrong lines** — verified against the file:

| Task | Cited | Actually says | Correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.4 | `:161` | `uses: actions/checkout@…` | `:153` |
| 3.6 | `:158-161` | `egress-policy` + checkout | `:149-153` |
| 1.3 | `:131` | `QUAY_ROBOT_TOKEN:` | `:115` |
| 5.3 | `:151` | `- flutter-android` | `:143` |

An implementer following 1.4 or 3.6 literally edits the checkout step. These are line drifts from reading `sed` windows without re-anchoring — my error, not the reviewer's.

**3. The Scout exclusion requirement is unimplementable as specified.** My own delta forbids both available mechanisms: `spec.md:108` says an image "SHALL NOT be excluded by being absent from a list", and `spec.md:11` says the file "SHALL carry image names only" — so no per-step flag. That leaves a hardcoded filter (forbidden by `:10`, "SHALL NOT restate the set inline") or a field in the file (forbidden by `:11`). The one job that motivated #506 has no legal implementation.

### Warnings

1. The `ci-image-tag-lifecycle` delta adds a new scenario (*"One image's cleanup failure does not skip another's"*) inside a MODIFIED block, implying `fail-fast: false` that no task states

5. Nothing verifies the `flutter-windows` Docker Hub repo exists before `update-description` targets it — failure would surface during a release

### The fix

Finding 3 is the interesting one, because it invalidates a decision **I talked you into**. I argued the name-list down from a tuple by auditing consumers — but I audited *current* consumers, and the exclusion is new behavior with no consumer yet. `linux-image-build-boundary:70-74` constrains *build arguments*; post-publish scope isn't one, so `[{name, scout: false}]` was never actually forbidden. input.content:
## Context

Three post-publish jobs enumerate the published image set by hand, and three
have drifted (`release.yml:184-186`, `:235-237`, `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26`).
PR #540 fixed the same defect on the build side with a shared composite action;
post-publish has no equivalent. Full findings in `research.md`.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- Adding an image costs one entry in one file, not a matrix edit per job.
- A post-publish step covering only some images derives that from the
  declaration, not from a list of its own.
- `flutter-windows`'s Scout exclusion is a declared fact with a recorded
  reason.

**Non-Goals:**

- Build-phase enumeration. `linux-image-build-boundary` owns it.
- Folding in `docker-compose.yml` and `docs/build.mjs`, which enumerate images
  correctly today.
- Adding a Windows-capable vulnerability scanner (researched, rejected —
  `proposal.md`).

## Decisions

### D1 — A separate file, not a key in `config/version.json`

`config/version.json` is validated by `#Version`, whose every member is a tool
version (`config/schema.cue:41-57`). An image set is not a version. It is also
written by machine: `update-version.yml` composes the manifest from three job
outputs via `jq` overlays (`:348-375`), and the image set has no producer in
that pipeline.

A top-level `. + $block` overlay was verified not to disturb a sibling key, so
co-locating would have been *safe* — the objection is naming, not mechanics. A
file called `version.json` holding a member that is not a version misleads the
next reader.

Cost: one CUE definition and one read. Accepted.

### D2 — Entries carry name plus post-publish scope, not build inputs

An audit of every consumer found `name` is the only field the post-publish jobs
use (30 `matrix.name` references; `update-description` and `record-image`
matrices carry no second field). `dockerfile` and `runner` have zero readers —
`build-linux-image/action.yml:68` hardcodes the Dockerfile path, and every
`runs-on:` in the repo is a literal. `target` has three readers, all in Linux
*build* legs, which `linux-image-build-boundary` owns.

So the entry carries `name`, plus scope for post-publish steps that do not
cover every image.

The scope field is required, not speculative: the exclusion requirement forbids
excluding an image by omitting it from the declaration, and forbids a step
carrying its own list. Without a declared scope there is no legal mechanism
left. This was the reasoning missed on the first pass — the consumer audit
covered *current* consumers, and the exclusion is new behavior with no consumer
yet.

`linux-image-build-boundary/spec.md:70-74` is not violated. It forbids routing
*build arguments* through a shared structure, because two manifest values
collide once flattened into env (`windows.git.version` vs `android.Dockerfile`'s
`ARG GIT_VERSION`, a Debian apt pin) and BuildKit only warns on an undeclared
arg. Post-publish scope never becomes a `--build-arg` and never enters that
namespace.

### D3 — Two questions, two sources: the declaration and the producing job

`ci-image-anonymous-availability` requires `verify-published` to verify exactly
what a run published, so a Windows-only `workflow_dispatch` verifies Windows
only. A declaration alone cannot satisfy that — a static file cannot shrink to
what a partial run published.

Both hold, because they answer different questions:

| Question | Source |
|---|---|
| Which images exist? | `config/images.json` |
| Which did *this run* publish? | the producing job's result |

`verify-published` enumerates candidates from the declaration and keeps each
leg gated on its producer. That is why `windows-image.yml` must declare
`outputs:` first — today it answers neither question, so post-publish steps
either hand-copy the Windows image's name or omit it.

The constraint that `verify-published` introduce no `needs:` edge between the
release jobs survives: it already declares `needs: [release-linux,
release-windows]` (`release.yml:140`), which is an edge from verification to
each, not between them.

### D4 — Where validation runs

Follows `validate-version-manifest`'s split: a composite action for consumers,
inline `cue vet` for producers. That action hardcodes its file and schema
(`action.yml`'s `cue vet config/schema.cue -d '#Version' config/version.json`),
so it cannot validate a second file unchanged. Two options, decided at
implementation:

- Add inputs (schema path, definition, data file) to the existing action, and
  have both call sites pass them. One action, two callers.
- Add a second action alongside it.

Preferred: parameterize the existing one, since the two invocations differ only
in three strings. Deferred rather than decided here because it depends on
whether any caller validates both files in one step.

## Open Questions

1. **Is a digest output obtainable from the Windows build?** The Windows path
   uses plain `docker build` (`windows-image.yml:151`), not buildx, so there is
   no `steps.build.outputs.digest`. Name and tag are free — both are already
   computed (`:39`, `:92`). A digest would need a `docker inspect` step, which
   is a real cost on a Windows runner for a value no consumer has asked for
   yet. Resolve at task 1.2 by naming a consumer or omitting it.

2. **Does the `flutter-windows` Docker Hub repository exist?** Description sync
   is being extended to it, and `peter-evans/dockerhub-description` fails if
   the repository is absent. The image is published to Docker Hub
   (`windows-image.yml:92-94`), so the repository should exist — but this is
   unverified, and the failure would surface during a release. Check before
   task 3.5.

## Risks / Trade-offs

**[`fromJSON` matrices are unproven here]** → Verified locally with `jq` (valid
payload, single-line `GITHUB_OUTPUT` round-trip, parses under `fromJSON`) but
never in a live Actions run. Task 1.4 proves it on `verify-published` alone,
before PR 3 makes four jobs depend on it.

**[A matrix-emitting job becomes a new `needs:` target]** → Every post-publish
job gains an edge to whatever reads the declaration. That is a new
single-point-of-failure for the post-publish phase. Accepted: the job is a file
read and a `cue vet`, and its failure means the declaration is invalid — in
which case fanning out over it would be wrong anyway.

**[Behaviour change is intentionally not uniform]** → Derived legs reproduce
today's matrices exactly for `record-image`, `verify-published`, and the build
legs. Only `update-description` (gains `flutter-windows`) and
`cleanup-pr-image` (gains `flutter-web`) differ — the two defects. Any third
difference is a regression.

## Migration Plan

Three PRs, split on real dependencies:

1. `windows-image.yml` outputs, plus `verify-published` reading the Windows
   name from them. Proves outputs and `fromJSON` on one job.
2. Tag-leak matrix and the one-off orphan sweep. Independent of 1 and 3.
3. `config/images.json`, post-publish fan-out, and the Scout exclusion.
   Requires 1.

Rollback: each PR is independently revertable. PR 3 is the only one that
changes which images a post-publish step covers.

content.text: Change 1 — the Scout exclusion. No declaration dependency, so C6 dissolves.

input.content:
## Why

`flutter-windows` has never been analyzed by Docker Scout. The `record-image`
job's matrix (`release.yml:235-237`) lists `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`
only, so no Scout environment record or CVE SARIF is produced for the Windows
image and it is absent from the code-scanning dashboard ([#506]).

[#506] asks to verify whether Scout produces meaningful output for a Windows
image before wiring it up. It does not, on three independent grounds — each
one disqualifying on its own:

1. **Architecture.** Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` only
   ([docs](https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/)). The published image
   is `os: windows, arch: amd64`, read from its registry config blob rather
   than inferred. Not fixable: Windows containers are `windows/amd64` by
   construction.
2. **Size.** The same limit is 4 GB compressed. The published image is
   **5.90 GB across 37 layers**, the `servercore` base alone being 1.42 GB.
3. **No advisory data, and no inventory to apply it to.** Scout's 23 advisory
   sources include no Microsoft/MSRC feed, and every OS ecosystem it supports
   is a Linux one
   ([sources](https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/)).
   Nor would another scanner help: `windows.Dockerfile` installs Git from a zip
   (`:20`), Flutter via `git clone` (`:42`), and VS Build Tools via an
   installer (`:74`). None is registered with a package manager, so an
   SBOM-driven scanner finds an empty inventory. Trivy's supported-OS table has
   no Windows row; Grype delegates cataloguing to Syft, which has no MSI or KB
   cataloger.

So the current behaviour is right and the omission is not a bug. What is wrong
is that nothing says so: the exclusion reads as an oversight, and the spec that
does mention it justifies it by the wrong thing (see below).

Relevance gate: this changes what a maintainer finds when they notice
`flutter-windows` missing from the code-scanning dashboard — a recorded
decision and a pointer to what does govern its CVE posture, instead of a gap
that invites the same investigation again.

## What Changes

- A new requirement in `windows-image-release` stating that `flutter-windows`
  is out of scope for Docker Scout, carrying all three disqualifiers, and
  naming what governs its CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image
  digest pin (`windows.Dockerfile:3`) and how promptly it is bumped. Microsoft
  rebuilds Windows base images monthly on Patch Tuesday.
- The existing *Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only* requirement
  is corrected. It currently justifies `record-image` skipping via
  `needs: release-android` (`spec.md:65`) — wrong twice over: no job named
  `release-android` exists (the code says `release-linux`, `release.yml:22`),
  and the skip is not produced by a `needs:` edge at all. Each downstream job
  carries an explicit `if: github.event_name == 'push' && !cancelled()` guard
  (`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284`), and under `!cancelled()` a skipped
  dependency does **not** auto-skip its dependents. The spec describes a
  mechanism the code does not use.
- A comment at `record-image`'s matrix recording the exclusion and its reason,
  so the omission is legible where someone would notice it.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Adding a Windows-capable scanner. Researched and rejected above.
- Any change to which images `record-image` actually records. Behaviour is
  unchanged; only its justification and legibility change.
- Declaring the published image set in a config file. That is a separate
  concern with its own defects to fix, and coupling it here is what made an
  earlier attempt at this change unreviewable.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `windows-image-release`: gains a requirement placing `flutter-windows` out of
  scope for Docker Scout on stated technical grounds; its
  `workflow_dispatch` requirement is corrected to describe the skip mechanism
  the code actually uses and to stop naming a job that does not exist.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/release.yml` (a comment at `record-image`'s
matrix, `:235-237`); `openspec/specs/windows-image-release/spec.md` on archive.

**No behaviour change.** `record-image`'s legs are identical before and after.
This change makes a decision legible and corrects a spec that misdescribes the
code; it does not alter what runs.

**Verification**: `record-image` runs on the next release with the same two
legs and the same SARIF categories. The spec correction is checked by reading
`release.yml:181`, `:232`, `:284` — the `if:` guards that actually produce the
dispatch skip.

**Risk**: low. The one judgement call is that the three disqualifiers are
durable. Architecture is structural; size has headroom in the wrong direction
(5.90 GB against 4 GB, and the image grows); the advisory-feed gap is
Docker's to close and would be announced. If Scout ever adds Windows support
the requirement should be revisited, not silently kept.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: The Windows image is out of scope for Docker Scout

`flutter-windows` SHALL NOT be recorded in Docker Scout, and the exclusion SHALL be justified by Scout's analysis support rather than by which job builds the image. The exclusion SHALL be recorded where `record-image`'s legs are listed, so a reader who notices the omission finds the decision at the point of omission.

Three independent facts each make the analysis impossible, and all three SHALL be recorded: Docker Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images only, while the published image is `windows/amd64`; the analysis size limit is 4 GB compressed, while the published image is 5.90 GB; and Scout carries no Microsoft advisory feed, while the image installs Git, the Flutter SDK, and VS Build Tools outside any package manager, so no SBOM-driven scanner finds an inventory to match against.

The record SHALL name what governs the Windows image's CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image digest pinned in `windows.Dockerfile` and how promptly that pin is bumped.

The experience context is the maintainer who notices `flutter-windows` absent from the code-scanning dashboard. They find a stated reason and a pointer to the control that does apply, instead of re-opening an investigation that has already been done. Before this requirement the omission was indistinguishable from an oversight, and was filed as a bug.

#### Scenario: The exclusion is stated, not implied by absence

- **GIVEN** a maintainer reads the job that records images in Docker Scout
- **WHEN** they ask why `flutter-windows` is not among its legs
- **THEN** the exclusion and its reason are recorded where the legs are listed
- **AND** the reason cites Scout's platform and size limits and its advisory coverage, not the release topology

#### Scenario: The Windows image is still covered by the other post-publish steps

- **GIVEN** `flutter-windows` is out of scope for Docker Scout
- **WHEN** a release publishes it
- **THEN** it is still verified as anonymously pullable

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Manual `workflow_dispatch` rebuild is Windows-only

The `release.yml` workflow SHALL continue to declare `workflow_dispatch:`. On `workflow_dispatch`, only the `release-windows` caller job SHALL execute; the Linux release job and the post-publish jobs (`update-description`, `record-image`, `create-github-release`) SHALL be skipped. The `FLUTTER_VERSION` env var SHALL be set from `github.ref_name`, so that a maintainer can rebuild a single tag's Windows image — through the same `windows-image.yml` reusable workflow — without re-cutting the Git tag and without re-publishing the Linux images, re-pushing the Docker Hub readme, or re-attempting `gh release create`.

Skipping SHALL be expressed as an explicit event guard on each job that must not run, not inferred from a `needs:` edge. A dependent job that declares `if: ... && !cancelled()` does not auto-skip when its dependency is skipped, so a `needs:` edge alone does not produce this behaviour.

The experience context is the maintainer recovering from a transient Windows runner failure: they re-run the workflow on the existing tag instead of force-pushing a new one. Linux recovery, by contrast, is the established fix-forward + re-tag pattern and does not need a `workflow_dispatch` path.

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild produces a fresh Windows image

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists in the repository
- **AND** the prior `release-windows` run for that tag failed
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the `release-windows` caller builds and pushes `flutter-windows:X.Y.Z` to all three registries via `windows-image.yml`
- **AND** the existing Windows image digests at those tags are overwritten by the new digests

#### Scenario: Manual rebuild leaves the Linux digests untouched

- **GIVEN** a tag `X.Y.Z` exists and was previously published with Android digest `D_a`
- **WHEN** a maintainer triggers `release.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` selecting ref `X.Y.Z`
- **THEN** the Linux release job is reported as `skipped`
- **AND** `update-description`, `record-image`, and `create-github-release` are reported as `skipped`
- **AND** each of those jobs is skipped by its own event guard, not by a `needs:` edge to a skipped job
- **AND** the digest at `docker.io/<org>/flutter-android:X.Y.Z` remains `D_a`
- **AND** the run is reported as success (no failed jobs)

## Why

PR builds push a `pr-<N>` handoff tag for **both** Linux images:
`build.yml`'s matrix covers `flutter-android` and `flutter-web` (`:48-55`), and
the GHCR ref is built from `matrix.name` (`:64`, `:132-138`). Cleanup deletes
one of them. `cleanup-pr-image.yml:26` hardcodes
`PACKAGE_NAME: flutter-android`, and that single name is what the two API calls
query (`:66`, `:82`).

So every closed PR leaves a `flutter-web:pr-<N>` tag behind. Counted against
GHCR on 2026-08-10:

| Package | Handoff tags present |
|---|---|
| `flutter-android` | 2 — both open PRs, expected |
| `flutter-web` | **22** — `pr-513` through `pr-543` |

Each orphan is a full image index carrying SBOM and provenance attestations
(`build.yml:151-155`), not a bare tag. The count grows by one per PR.

The spec has the same defect: `ci-image-tag-lifecycle`'s Purpose and both
deletion requirements are scoped to `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android`
(`spec.md:5,11,17,43`). The workflow matches its spec — the spec was written
when `flutter-android` was the only image and never revisited when
`flutter-web` was added.

Relevance gate: this changes what a maintainer finds when auditing GHCR
storage — one tag per open PR, as the capability already promises, rather than
one per ever-opened PR on an image nobody was cleaning.

## What Changes

- `cleanup-pr-image.yml` iterates the images that produce handoff tags instead
  of naming one, with `fail-fast: false` so one image's failure does not skip
  another's.
- The 22 existing `flutter-web` orphans are swept once. The workflow fires only
  on `pull_request: closed` and `delete`, so it will never revisit tags for
  PRs that are already closed.
- `ci-image-tag-lifecycle` is de-scoped from `flutter-android` — its Purpose
  and its two deletion requirements.

Explicitly **not** in scope:

- Declaring the published image set in a config file. The image list here is
  short, local, and about which images produce *handoff tags* — a narrower
  question than which images are published. If a declaration lands later this
  workflow is a natural consumer, but it is not a prerequisite.
- `flutter-windows`, which produces no handoff tags: `windows.yml` calls
  `windows-image.yml` with `push: false` (`windows.yml:19-22`), so a PR
  builds it without pushing anything to delete.
- The two image-agnostic requirements in the capability, *Cleanup never
  targets a non-handoff tag* (`spec.md:47`) and *Cleanup workflow runs with
  minimum privilege* (`:68`). Both already hold for any image.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities

- `ci-image-tag-lifecycle`: its two deletion requirements are de-scoped from
  `ghcr.io/<owner>/flutter-android` to every image that produces handoff tags,
  and gain the guarantee that one image's cleanup failure does not skip
  another's.

## Impact

**Modified**: `.github/workflows/cleanup-pr-image.yml` (matrix over the image
names, `fail-fast: false`); `openspec/specs/ci-image-tag-lifecycle/spec.md` on
archive, including its Purpose line (`:5`).

**One-off**: sweep the orphaned `flutter-web` handoff tags. Deletion must
resolve a specific `pr-<N>` tag to a version ID and delete by ID — a
`tags == []` filter would match OCI index children and break parent tags.

**Verification**: after the sweep, each package should carry handoff tags only
for open PRs. The next closed PR should leave neither image with a `pr-<N>`
tag.

**Risk**: the sweep is a destructive registry operation. It is bounded by the
existing tag-regex guard (`:49-52`), which refuses anything that is not
`pr-<N>` or `branch-<ref>`, keeping release tags and `buildcache` unreachable —
but the one-off sweep runs outside that workflow, so it needs the same guard
applied deliberately rather than inherited.

The two requirements not restated below, *Cleanup never targets a non-handoff tag* (`:47`) and *Cleanup workflow runs with minimum privilege* (`:68`), are image-agnostic already and are deliberately unmodified.

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: PR-close deletes the corresponding handoff tag

When a `pull_request` closes (merged or not), a workflow SHALL delete the GHCR tag `pr-<N>` corresponding to that PR number, on every image that produces handoff tags, if it exists.

Cleanup SHALL be independent per image: one image's deletion failing SHALL NOT prevent another's from being attempted.

The experience context is the maintainer auditing GHCR storage — they expect to see one tag per open PR, not per ever-opened PR, and not one image cleaned while another accumulates. Scoping cleanup to a single image is what let `flutter-web` reach 22 orphaned handoff tags while `flutter-android` stayed clean.

#### Scenario: Closing a merged PR removes the handoff tag from every image

- **GIVEN** PR #42 was opened on a same-repo branch, ran `build.yml`, and produced `pr-42` on both `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`
- **WHEN** PR #42 is merged
- **THEN** the cleanup workflow deletes `pr-42` from every image that produced it
- **AND** no image retains `pr-42` because cleanup did not name it

#### Scenario: Closing an unmerged PR removes the handoff tag

- **GIVEN** PR #42 produced `pr-42` and is closed without merging
- **WHEN** the cleanup workflow runs
- **THEN** `pr-42` is deleted from every image that produced it

#### Scenario: Cleanup is idempotent when the tag does not exist

- **GIVEN** PR #42 is from a fork (the artifact path was used; no GHCR tag was created)
- **WHEN** PR #42 closes and the cleanup workflow runs
- **THEN** each leg logs "tag not found, nothing to delete"
- **AND** the workflow exits 0 (does not fail)

#### Scenario: One image's cleanup failure does not skip another's

- **GIVEN** cleanup runs for several images and one image's deletion fails
- **WHEN** the workflow completes
- **THEN** the remaining images' handoff tags have still been deleted
- **AND** only the failing leg is reported red

### Requirement: Branch deletion deletes the corresponding branch handoff tag

When a branch is deleted (`delete` event with `ref_type == 'branch'`), the cleanup workflow SHALL delete the GHCR tag `branch-<branch-name>` (with `/` → `-`) if it exists, on every image that produces handoff tags.

The experience context is the maintainer running `workflow_dispatch` on a feature branch, then deleting the branch — they expect the `branch-<name>` tag to disappear automatically, from every image that built it, not only from the one the workflow happens to name.

#### Scenario: Branch deletion removes the branch handoff tag from every image

- **GIVEN** branch `feature/new-cache` was tested via `workflow_dispatch`, producing `branch-feature-new-cache` on every image that produces handoff tags
- **WHEN** the branch is deleted
- **THEN** the cleanup workflow computes `branch-feature-new-cache` from the deleted ref and deletes it from each image

Three independent facts each make the analysis impossible, and all three SHALL be recorded with enough detail to be re-derived:

| Fact | Source |
|---|---|
| Scout analyses `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images only; the published image is `windows/amd64` | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/>; image platform from the registry config blob for the published tag |
| Scout's analysis size limit is 4 GB compressed; the published image is 5.90 GB | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/policy/scores/>; size from summing layer sizes in the published tag's manifest |
| Scout carries no Microsoft advisory feed, and the image installs Git, the Flutter SDK, and VS Build Tools outside any package manager, so no SBOM-driven scanner finds an inventory to match | <https://docs.docker.com/scout/deep-dive/advisory-db-sources/>; install mechanisms visible in `windows.Dockerfile` |

The exclusion SHALL hold only while those facts hold. If Docker Scout adds Windows image support, raises the size limit above the published image's size, or adds a Microsoft advisory feed, this requirement SHALL be revisited rather than carried forward unexamined.

The record SHALL name what governs the Windows image's CVE posture instead: the `servercore` base-image digest pinned in `windows.Dockerfile`, and the cadence at which that pin is bumped.

content.text:
## First: the Renovate correction

PR #542 refutes my claim. Renovate **does** bump the `servercore` digest — weekly, with automerge, four times in history (#542, #435, #428, #425). My grep looked for an explicit `mcr.microsoft.com` rule, but none is needed: `config:recommended` enables the built-in `dockerfile` manager, and `renovate.json` disables only `github-actions`. I inferred absence of a rule meant absence of coverage.

Updated: the requirement now names Renovate as the live control, the proposal cites the evidence, and task 4.2 dropped that half — it's now only the stale `release-android` name in `ci-image-anonymous-availability`. Worktree also synced to `ae870a0`, and all three changes re-anchored (citations verified unchanged).

## Review result: APPROVED_WITH_WARNINGS — `pr-tag-cleanup-all-images`

**Criteria source:** all three loaded. Marker written.

**Zero CRITICALs.** All citations verified at `ae870a0`. Two things the reviewer checked harder than I did:

- **The `flutter-windows` exclusion is right** — verified past my citation: `windows-image.yml:154-155` gates the push on `inputs.push`, and the metadata action emits only the version tag. GHCR confirms zero `pr-*` tags on that package.
- **Delete-by-version-ID is genuinely necessary** — `flutter-web` has ~90 untagged versions (index children, attestations) alongside ~90 tagged. A `tags == []` filter would sweep them. Also confirmed no version carries more than one tag, so resolving a `pr-N` tag can't collaterally hit a release tag.

**W1 was a real error of mine, not staleness.** I claimed `flutter-android` "stayed clean." It hasn't:

| Package | Handoff tags | Orphans |
|---|---|---|
| `flutter-android` | 4 | **3** — `pr-454/455/456` |
| `flutter-web` | 33 | **32** — `pr-489`…`pr-543` |

Only #533 is open. So the android image *is* covered by the workflow and still has residue — a second, smaller defect with a different cause. My sweep was scoped to `flutter-web` only and would have left them, making task 2.7's own check fail. Both the proposal and the spec's experience context repeated the false premise; both fixed, and the sweep now covers both packages.

Also applied: **W2** removed the misplaced preamble (duplicated `tasks.md:3.1`), **W3** added a concrete open-PR re-check before DELETEs — a PR opening mid-sweep would otherwise have its tag deleted under a running build — and **W4/S1/S3** as smaller edits.

Two threads filed rather than fixed: `ci-image-handoff` hardcodes `flutter-android` while `web-image-testing:52` asserts `flutter-web:pr-<N>` exists — those two main specs contradict each other today, independent of this work.

`windows-description-sync` is the last one unreviewed.

Yes — we are creating them, on a live and reachable path.

`build.yml` triggers on `pull_request` **and** `workflow_dispatch` (`:4-5`). The handoff computation at `:118-125` is a plain if/else on `IS_PR`: PR → `pr-<N>`, **everything else → `branch-<ref>`**. There's no third branch and no guard. The push at `:145` is gated only on `is_fork != 'true'`, which a `workflow_dispatch` always satisfies (`IS_FORK` is hardcoded false unless the event is a `pull_request`). So any manual `build.yml` run on a branch pushes `branch-<ref>` to GHCR for both `flutter-android` and `flutter-web`.

The reason zero exist right now is simply that nobody has dispatched `build.yml` from a non-`main` branch recently enough to survive — not that the path is dead. And note the `else` catches `main` too: a dispatch from the default branch produces `branch-main`.

This sharpens the earlier finding rather than reversing it. What I said was that the `branch-` requirement was "spec'd as though observed" with no subject. Half of that stands and half doesn't:

- **The producer is real and correctly matrixed.** `build.yml:124` sits inside the `build-image` job, which already matrixes both images (`:48-55`). So a dispatch leaks `branch-<ref>` on *both* packages — exactly the systemic gap the change fixes. The delta's "on every image that produces handoff tags" is right on the merits.
- **The cleanup side has a real asymmetry the change doesn't address.** `cleanup-pr-image.yml:44` reconstructs the tag from the deleted branch's `REF_NAME`. That fires on a `delete` event — which never happens for `main`, and doesn't happen for a branch that's dispatched-then-merged-then-auto-deleted only if the delete event actually lands. So `branch-main` is unreachable by cleanup by construction: nothing ever deletes `main`. It would sit in GHCR permanently.

That last point is worth folding in, because it's the same class of defect as the one we're already fixing (a producer whose consumer doesn't cover it), and it's cheap to state. It doesn't change the matrix work in group 1.

Applied. Change validates strict; task IDs are sequential and unique.

**What changed:**

| File | Edit |
|---|---|
